title: Routing and Path Selection Concepts
summary: Reason about routes, next hops, and path preference without configuring production routers.
objectives: Distinguish local switching from routing between networks.
Interpret a simplified routing table, default route, next hop, and path preference.

vocab.def: The next routing destination used to move traffic toward another network.
A fallback route used when no more specific route matches.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: Routing is studied with synthetic tables only. Do not configure, scan, or access real network equipment.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: A switch forwards within a local network; a router selects a path between networks. In a synthetic table, choose the most specific matching route, then consider its next hop and stated preference. Static and dynamic routing are concepts here, not production configuration tasks.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Explain why a selected route matches the destination and identify what the table does not establish.

practice.prompt: How is routing different from switching?
practice.answer: Switching forwards within a local network; routing selects paths between networks.

quiz.question: When does a default route apply in a simplified table?
options: When no more specific route matches
Only when a cable is unplugged
quiz.answer: When no more specific route matches

lab.objective: Interpret a synthetic routing table and path choice.

reflectionPrompt: What evidence supported the selected next hop?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
